THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA No.200903/2019 is filed by the Road Transport Corporation (henceforth referred to as 'Corporation') challenging the finding regarding negligence on the part of the driver of bus belonging to it as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur (henceforth referred as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.14/2017, vide judgment and award dated 05.01.2019.

entities.text: I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.201194/2019 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in the aforesaid case.

3. The deceased, a driver in an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-36/A-9183 died in a road accident on 29.05.2016 when the autorickshaw driven by him was rear ended by a bus belonging to the Corporation bearing NC: 2023:KHC-K:5555 registration No.KA-37/F-559.
The claimant claimed that the deceased was 34 years old and an agriculturist and also used to drive the autorickshaw and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

They claimed that they were deprived of emotional and financial support and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation from the driver of the bus and the Corporation.
4. The Corporation contested the claim petition and contended that the deceased was negligent and was driving the autorickshaw negligently on the road.
It denied any negligence on the part of its driver.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked documents as Exs.P1 to P7.
Driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation was examined as RW.1.

sentences.text: Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation.
It also held that the deceased died in the accident.

It considered the evidence of the claimant No.1 and NC:
2023:KHC-K:5555 held that the deceased was 35 years old at the time of the accident and considered his notional income at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation:-
 Sl

. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 7,68,000/-
 2 Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-
 3 Loss of estate 25,000/-
 4 Loss of consortium 10,000/-
 5

Funeral expenses 25,000/-
 Total 9,28,000/-
Less : Interim compensation 15,000/-

Total 9,13,000/-
In so far as liability is concerned, the Tribunal held that the Corporation is liable to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
7.
Being aggrieved by the finding regarding the negligence, the Corporation has filed MFA No.200903/209.

Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
the claimants have filed MFA No.201194/2019.
The learned counsel for the Corporation submitted that the deceased was negligent and was responsible for the accident and the evidence of RW.1 clearly established the same.
She contended that the Tribunal blindly accepted the case of the claimants without considering the evidence of RW.1.
She further contended that the Tribunal awarded excessive compensation under the conventional heads and prays that the same may be re-determined.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, while in similar circumstances, the notional income is considered at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
He further contended that the deceased was a driver and PW.1 had marked copy of the licence as Ex.P7.
He therefore, contended that the income of the deceased must have been considered at not less than Rs.10,000/- per month.

He also contended that the Tribunal failed to award loss of future prospects at 40% as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Corporation and the learned counsel for the claimants.
11. The fact that the accident happened on 29.05.2016 at 11.30 a.m. is not much in dispute.

It is also not in dispute that the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation rear ended the autorickshaw resulting in autorickshaw over turning and causing death of the deceased and injuries to other passengers.

Therefore, the Corporation cannot contend that the driver of the autorickshaw was negligent, as it was the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation who must have exercised due care and caution while driving a heavy vehicle on the road.
In that view of the matter, the finding regarding the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation is unexceptionable.

12. In so far as quantum of compensation is concerned, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the notional income of the deceased must have been considered at Rs.8,750/- per month.
In addition, the claimants were entitled to loss of future prospects at 40% of the notional income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi, supra.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Towards loss of dependency 15,68,000/-
 (8,750 + 40% x 12 x 16 x 2/3)
 2 Towards loss of spousal 44,000/-
 consortium  3 Towards loss of estate and funeral 33,000/-
 expenses  Total 16,45,000/-
 Less : Interim compensation 15,000/-
As regard the liability to pay the compensation, it is the bus belonging to the Corporation that was driven by the driver in rash and negligent manner.
Therefore, the liability to pay the compensation is upon the Corporation.

Consequently, the Corporation/appellant in MFA No.200903/2019 is liable to pay the compensation determined by this Court along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
15. In view of the above, the appeal filed by the Corporation in MFA No.200903/2019 is dismissed.
The appeal filed by the claimants in MFA No.201194/2019 is allowed in NC: 2023:KHC-K:5555 part.

The compensation of Rs.9,13,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.16,30,000/-, which is payable by the Corporation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum The Divisional Controller vs Gangamma And Ors on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162563425/
5 from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: 16. The compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
17. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.1 in any nationalized Bank for a period of five years.

Out of the balance, 30% shall be released to the claimant No.3 and remaining shall be released in favour of claimant No.2.
18.
The amount in deposit by the Corporation in MFA No.200903/2019 is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
